step1.text: The user configures Rhea as the lead and four peers across different providers
step1.evidence: core scenario story: Rhea leads; Mira and Nico on Codex, Oren on OpenCode, Pia on Grok Build, Quinn on Antigravity (four peers across different providers, plus a second Codex peer so the story can hold a sibling clarification)

step2.text: All employees begin dormant; one is disabled
step2.evidence: core scenario story: roster.get shows four dormant and Quinn disabled before any session starts

step3.text: The user starts a project conversation with Rhea
step3.evidence: core scenario story: the conversation is created in a registered project (a temporary git repository with a base commit) and led by Rhea

step4.text: Rhea receives a current roster and proposes a multi-part plan
step4.evidence: core scenario story: employees_list then two task_delegate calls inside the lead turn, and a third in a follow-up turn once the first plan finished

step5.text: Under ask mode, Lazoo presents precise delegation approvals
step5.evidence: core scenario story: both children are proposed, counted by the Inbox, and accepted by the user; provider permission approvals are approval-gate.ps1

step6.text: Approved employees activate into independent native sessions and editing worktrees
step6.evidence: core scenario story: each accepted task runs on a fresh session for Mira started inside its own retained git worktree of the project (never the canonical checkout), the session stops with its turn, and the next queued task wakes when she is free

step7.text: An employee asks a peer a direct clarification without routing through Rhea
step7.evidence: core scenario story: inside her dispatch turn Mira asks Nico through message_send and waits; Nico, waiting on her task in task_wait, receives the question in that wait and answers through message_reply; her wait returns his answer; the ledger holds the question on his task and the reply on hers; no peer turn reaches Rhea; peer-messaging.ps1 and coalesced-notices.ps1 prove the lead-recipient path and the idle-session delivery

step8.text: The disabled employee is not selected and cannot receive dispatch
step8.evidence: core scenario story: task_delegate to Quinn is refused LZ-TASK-ASSIGNEE-UNAVAILABLE and writes nothing

step9.text: One provider stalls after accepting work; Lazoo detects missing progress, retries safely, then raises a clean incident
step9.evidence: core scenario story: the third task dispatch turn stalls (the adapter progress deadline reported as a stalled provider error, as opencode_acceptance_without_progress_becomes_stalled proves for the real adapter), the turn is recorded retryable-failed, the task stays accepted for a bounded retry by the lead or the user and is never retried automatically, the worker session is stopped, and one LZ-SESSION-STALLED incident on the task is raised and promoted at once

step10.text: The threshold notifies Rhea, allows bounded remediation, and escalates to the user when unresolved
step10.evidence: core scenario story: the stall on the queued third task opens the lead window, the lead cancels it in its notice turn, the stall recurs, the sweep escalates to the user, and the user acknowledges it from the Inbox

step11.text: Lazoo restarts during an in-flight message and reconciles without losing or duplicating the logical task
step11.evidence: core scenario story restarts with the prior boot owner-lost and every task kept once; the in-flight attempt is message_restart_reconciles_an_uncertain_attempt in collaboration-bus.ps1 and native-session-ownership.ps1

step12.text: Results include commits, verification, task links, messages, incidents, and concise memory records
step12.evidence: core scenario story: the first worker reports completion through task_report with commit and verification evidence, which is the task's durable evidence through task.show, and the result notice links the task; messages and incidents are ledgers of their own (result-delivery.ps1, minimum-incidents.ps1); on the restarted daemon the completed task's dispatch turn is archived through memory.archive, a dedicated dormant Codex summary employee opted in through memory.worker.configure summarizes it in one fresh read-only turn, and the typed memory record citing that turn and the archive's source hash is read back through memory.search by taskId (the summary output is scripted on the fake transport: the worker pipeline is proven, model summary quality is not)

step13.text: Integration follows configured authority and never overwrites dirty user work
step13.evidence: core scenario story: every task runs under the ask authority the user configured, each worktree starts from the committed base, and the dirty edit in the canonical checkout is untouched after both dispatches; project_task_dispatch_uses_an_isolated_worktree_and_preserves_dirty_user_files (automatic-task-dispatch.ps1) proves the same with a running provider turn

step14.text: Employees return to idle and suspend after policy timeout
step14.evidence: core scenario story: Mira idles after warm and is suspended once her one-minute timeout passes

step15.text: Lazoo remains inside its measured resource budget
